The discussion outlines the local Ollama configuration at http://localhost:11434 used within convmem for embedding and summarization tasks. Embeddings are generated using nomic-embed-text to create search vectors, while llama3.1:8b handles summary generation when running locally without external API keys. For synthesis or distillation paths, the system prioritizes deepseek-v4-flash via the DeepSeek API if DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is set, falling back to local llama3.1:8b otherwise for a one-line switch capability.
Keywords: Ollama, convmem, nomic-embed-text, llama3.1:8b, deepseek-v4-flash, DeepSeek API, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, localhost:11434

The discussion focused on a `/wp-login.php` returning HTTP status code 404 within staging2 because SiteGround Security plugin slug renaming conflicted with the custom override in `wh-local-dev`. To resolve this, the login path was reconfigured directly inside the SiteGround Security settings to ensure it matched the specific development environment requirements. A successful redirect test validated the fix after updating the configuration, and the troubleshooting session was recorded with identifier `dec_prop_20260624_025115_862b`.

Keywords: wp-login.php, staging2, SiteGround Security plugin, wh-local-dev, slug override, 404 error, redirect test, dec_prop_20260624_025115_862b

We implemented a Thai Massage card morph on willowyhollow using the cross-document View Transition API via document.startViewTransition. A shared view-transition-name was configured between the home card and dedicated page to facilitate a smooth transition effect utilizing a cubic-bezier fade-forward curve. This implementation improved perceived performance and reduced Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) metrics across the application.
Keywords: willowyhollow, Thai Massage card morph, View Transition API, document.startViewTransition, view-transition-name, cubic-bezier fade-forward curve, Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS), cross-document transition
